summary:
H.R. 8997, the "Energy and Water Development and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2025," is the House Committee on Appropriations' reported general appropriations bill providing discretionary funding for FY2025 (ending September 30, 2025) across five titles. Most appropriations are made "to remain available until expended," with certain administrative and program-direction accounts limited to availability through September 30, 2026.

**Title I (Corps of Engineers—Civil)** appropriates funds under Department of the Army supervision, including $159 million (Investigations), $3.01 billion (Construction, with specified derivations from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund and Inland Waterways Trust Fund), $370 million (Mississippi River and Tributaries), $5.714 billion (Operation and Maintenance, drawing on the HMTF and referencing 33 U.S.C. 2238c(c) and CARES Act §14003), $218 million (Regulatory Program), $200 million (FUSRAP), $45 million (Flood Control and Coastal Emergencies), and administrative accounts. General provisions (§§101–112) impose reprogramming thresholds, transfer authority (§104, up to $8,733,000 to FWS), and substantive limitations, including firearm-possession protections at Corps projects (§110) and prohibitions on funding open-lake dredged-material placement absent §401 CWA certification (§105) and on enforcing §370 of Public Law 116-283 (§112).

**Title II (Interior—Central Utah Project and Bureau of Reclamation)** appropriates $23 million (CUP), $1.773 billion (Water and Related Resources), CVP Restoration Fund collections, $33 million (California Bay-Delta), and $66.794 million (Policy and Administration, from the Reclamation Fund). Notably, it amends authorization ceilings: §203 extends the CALFED Act sunset to 2025 and raises §103(f)(4)(A) to $40 million; §204 extends and raises Reclamation States Emergency Drought Relief Act authorizations; §§207–209 amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (43 U.S.C. 3202) and WIIN Act (Public Law 114-322), extending sunsets (e.g., §4013 to December 16, 2034) and raising authorizations in 43 U.S.C. 390h ($167.5 million) and the Water Desalination Act ($100.5 million). Sections 205–206 restrict CVP/SWP consultation activities under ESA §7.

**Title III (Department of Energy)** provides major appropriations including Weapons Activities ($20.339 billion), Science ($8.39 billion), Defense Environmental Cleanup ($7.132 billion), Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation ($2.445 billion), Naval Reactors ($2.119 billion), Nuclear Energy ($1.793 billion), EERE ($1.96 billion), and Power Marketing Administrations. Section 315 amends Natural Gas Act §3 (15 U.S.C. 717b), vesting FERC with exclusive authority over LNG export/import facility siting and deeming such trade consistent with the public interest, subject to a Presidential sanctions savings clause. Section 317 transfers specified unobligated IIJA and Public Law 117-169 balances to Nuclear Energy for SMR and reactor demonstration projects and amends Public Law 117-169 authorization amounts.

**Titles IV–V** fund independent agencies (NRC, DNFSB, regional commissions) and impose government-wide restrictions, including prohibitions on funds for CRT (§505), specified equity Executive Orders (§506), COVID-19 mandates (§508), the Wuhan Institute of Virology (§509), and several DOE energy-conservation rules (§514). Section 515 sets the spending reduction account at $0.
